summary: DB-016 authored the CP-110 remedy for the split-brain authorization defect: one additive, forward-only migration that seeds the workforce.* capability slice into public.org_role_permissions for the twelve ROLE_DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES roles, so public.has_perm and the TypeScript capability gate stop disagreeing. A legitimate organization administrator previously PASSED withAdminCapability('workforce.manage') and then read ZERO rows. The authoring lane proved the defect live and the fix closed on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster (64 PASS / 0 FAIL, twice) and never applied anything (CP-051). READ THE NAMED COST FIRST: this apply INVALIDATES EVERY ACTIVE ACTING-CONTEXT SESSION, and re-activation verification is a PREFLIGHT step, not a follow-up.

operator_manifest.order: Apply this file ALONE, once, on top of whatever the target's migration history already reflects. Do NOT apply it as part of a chain replay, a `supabase migration up` over the whole directory, a `supabase db push --include-all`, a forced apply, or a `supabase db reset`. CP-051: migrations are applied manually, one at a time, reviewed and explicit. Nothing in this file depends on another migration being applied first, and nothing it does requires another migration to follow. All twelve roles are in THIS ONE file on purpose: two applies would mean two session-invalidation windows.

the_named_cost_read_this_before_anything.what: admin_acting_context_sessions.capability_version is encode(digest(concat_ws('|', v_role, array_to_string(v_perms, ',')), 'sha256'), 'hex') (20260722002848:180-183), and the same expression is RE-CHECKED on every use of the session (20260722002848:317-320). Mutating a role's perms therefore invalidates every active acting-context session for members of that role.
the_named_cost_read_this_before_anything.how_much_it_costs: This file writes each role's perms as a SORTED, DE-DUPLICATED union. The digest is over the array IN ORDER, so the digest changes for EVERY role the file touches - including for permissions that were already granted, because the array is re-ordered. 'Only the new permissions change the digest' is the WRONG answer and would leave an operator under-counting the affected sessions. admin_current_acting_context recomputes the digest from the same expression, so the sort itself is behaviourally inert; what breaks is every existing session row, because its stored capability_version no longer matches.
the_named_cost_read_this_before_anything.what_to_do_about_it: VERIFIED BEFORE THE APPLY, NOT AFTER. Preflight step 3 counts the live sessions. Step 4 walks a real user through the re-activation path and confirms a fresh session carries the new digest. Apply only when step 4 has passed. If step 4 cannot be walked, STOP - do not apply and discover the cost in production.
the_named_cost_read_this_before_anything.who_is_affected: Every signed-in admin who has an active acting context in ANY organization whose members hold one of the twelve roles. That is every organization on the platform with an active admin session, which is why the count belongs in the release ticket and not only in the apply log.

what_the_file_does: One transaction. A DO block that first asserts preconditions: public.org_role_permissions exists, perms is text[] NOT NULL, org_members.org_members_permissions_check exists AND is VALIDATED, and its rendered text admits all three of workforce.view / workforce.manage / workforce.publish.

Snapshots the whole matrix as JSONb into a plpgsql variable. This is the pre-state every additivity assertion is measured against, which is why no temporary table is created and nothing is left in any schema on commit.

Upserts all twelve roles with a SORTED, DE-DUPLICATED UNION of whatever the target already holds and the declared workforce.* slice. A role with no row is created with just its slice; for ticketing, ticketing_manager and worker that slice is empty, so the new row is perms = '{}', which is behaviourally identical to the absent row it replaces (has_perm coalesces a missing matrix row to an empty array at 20260821180438:148).

In the SAME transaction, asserts: no pre-existing permission was removed (measured against the snapshot); no role was created outside the declared seed; department_manager does NOT carry workforce.manage; the seed literal names nothing outside the governed workforce vocabulary; and each role's workforce.* slice EQUALS the declared slice.
what_it_does_not_touch: No table, column, index, constraint, trigger, policy or function. This is a DATA change in one existing table, which is also why lib/database.types.ts needs no regeneration - the generated contract describes shape and no shape changed.
No row in any other table is read for update or deleted. Every org_members row, every staff_members row, every admin_acting_context_sessions row is left exactly as it was.
The capability catalog, the resolver, and every route. No TypeScript file is modified by this task. types/vendor-identity-contract.ts (WFC-003's derivation) is imported READ-ONLY by the test.
No per-tenant delegation, no department table, no department-scoped RLS path, no second membership or role table, no new permission vocabulary. WFC-004 owns the workforce schema.

The non-workforce capabilities. The matrix still lacks tour.view, event.view, logistics.*, finance.view, ticketing.*, site_map.* and content.* for every role, so the application gate remains a superset of the matrix for those. That is 206 measured (role, capability) pairs and it is a NEW decision reserved to WFC-003, not something this migration absorbs.

the_exact_perms_change_per_role.department_manager: NEW ROW, created with workforce.publish and workforce.view AND DELIBERATELY NOT workforce.manage. Withholding is the posture, not an oversight: has_perm(uid, oid, perm) has no target argument, so any permission in this table is granted across the WHOLE organization, and workforce.manage is department-scoped for this role (lib/auth/admin-capabilities.ts:319-323). Seeding it would hand a department manager organization-wide management authority, which is exactly what CP-094 forbids. If you find yourself wanting to add it, that is the bug, not the fix.
the_exact_perms_change_per_role.ticketing: NEW ROW, created with an EMPTY perms array, which is behaviourally identical to the absent row it replaces.
the_exact_perms_change_per_role.ticketing_manager: NEW ROW, created with an EMPTY perms array.
the_exact_perms_change_per_role.worker: NEW ROW, created with an EMPTY perms array. A worker still reads their own staff_members row through staff_members_worker_read_own; this migration does not touch that policy.

preflight_read_only_run_first: SELECT role, perms FROM public.org_role_permissions ORDER BY role;
SELECT r.role, p.perm FROM public.org_role_permissions r, unnest(r.perms) AS p(perm) WHERE p.perm LIKE 'workforce.%' ORDER BY r.role, p.perm;
SELECT count(*) AS acting_context_sessions, count(*) FILTER (WHERE revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now()) AS live_sessions FROM public.admin_acting_context_sessions;
SELECT c.relrowsecurity, c.relforcerowsecurity FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname = 'public' AND c.relname IN ('org_role_permissions','org_members');
SELECT conname, convalidated, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'public.org_members'::regclass AND conname = 'org_members_permissions_check';
SELECT policyname, polcmd, polpermissive, polroles::regrole[], qual FROM pg_policies WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND tablename = 'org_role_permissions' ORDER BY policyname;
operator_manifest.preflight_capture_for_rollback: Record the result of preflight query 1 VERBATIM, per role, including the exact array order. The rollback is a data write and needs the pre-apply arrays; a blind `perms = array_remove(perms, 'workforce.*')` is NOT a rollback, because it would also strip a workforce permission the target legitimately held beforehand, which is exactly what this migration's additivity assertion exists to prevent.
stop_conditions: STOP if preflight query 2 returns any row. A target that already grants a workforce.* permission to a role CP-102 does not grant it to will make the migration's exact-membership assertion ABORT the apply. That abort is correct and is the point: it means the target has drifted from the chain, which DB-002 recorded is possible because some hosted versions were applied by raw Management API SQL. Route it back to database. Do NOT work around it by editing the seed, and do NOT 'fix' it by removing the drifted permission in the same run.

STOP if you have NOT walked the acting-context re-activation path before applying. This apply invalidates every active acting-context session (see the_named_cost). Discovering that in production, from a support ticket, is the failure this step exists to prevent.

STOP if `authenticated_can_execute_has_perm` is false. has_perm is SECURITY DEFINER and the chain grants it to authenticated at 20260711153040:36, but grants are not managed uniformly. Without it, every workforce-governed RLS predicate ERRORS rather than denies - a different failure from a zero and a much louder one. Report it rather than accepting the apply.

STOP if the apply raises. The post-condition is inside the same transaction as the write, so a raise means the target could not reach the asserted state. Capture the message verbatim. Do NOT re-run with the post-condition removed, and do NOT split the file into twelve applies: one migration is what keeps the session-invalidation cost to a single window.

STOP if preflight query 1 shows a role name that is not one of the twelve, carrying a workforce.* permission. It is a custom role and its workforce authority is a configuration decision for WFC-005/ORG-007, not for this apply.
operator_manifest.postflight_contract: psql -f supabase/tests/db016_workforce_role_seed_contract.sql — expect ZERO violation rows and exactly one summary row rendering as: DB-016 workforce role seed | t. On a target that still holds the chain's own pre-state this file returns 8 violation rows and summary `f`, so a green result means the apply landed, not that the check is quiet.

what_a_correct_result_looks_like.headline_the_administrator_now_reads_row: As an organization administrator (role owner or admin) of the owning organization: `SELECT count(*) FROM public.staff_members;` returns that organization's row count, NOT 0. THIS IS THE PROBE THAT MATCHES THE DEFECT. Zero here is a FAILED APPLY, not a correct denial: the caller passed withAdminCapability('workforce.view') at app/api/admin/staff/route.ts:17 and must now receive rows. It returned 0 before the fix, which is the whole reason this migration exists.
what_a_correct_result_looks_like.the_administrator_can_write: As the same administrator, UPDATE a benign column on a row in your own organization -> UPDATE 1. UPDATE 0 means workforce.manage did not land and the apply is incomplete.
what_a_correct_result_looks_like.the_cp094_probe_department_manager: As a department_manager: `SELECT count(*) FROM public.staff_members WHERE org_id = '<your org>';` returns your organization's row count, because workforce.view is organization-wide for this role (ADMIN-012's explicit decision, lib/auth/admin-capabilities.ts:304-313). Then UPDATE one of those rows -> UPDATE 0. **UPDATE 1 IS A CP-094 VIOLATION.** Stop, roll forward, and page security-admin. This is the single change that would actually violate CP-094, and it is why the migration asserts its absence inside the transaction rather than trusting review.
what_a_correct_result_looks_like.cross_tenant_still_denied: As any caller holding workforce.view or workforce.manage: `SELECT count(*) FROM public.staff_members WHERE org_id = '<an organization you are not a member of>';` returns 0. THE QUERY SUCCEEDS — zero rows, not a permission error. An `ERROR: permission denied for table staff_members` here means the GRANT is missing, which is a different problem and not a pass.
what_a_correct_result_looks_like.no_widening_across_tenants: As the same administrator: `SELECT count(*) FROM public.staff_members WHERE org_id = '<another organization>';` -> 0. This migration widens WHO can read inside an organization, so this is the probe that proves it did not widen ACROSS organizations. If it returns rows, stop. The harness proved all twelve roles read only their own organization's rows.
what_a_correct_result_looks_like.the_vocabulary_probe: SELECT r.role, p.perm FROM public.org_role_permissions r, unnest(r.perms) p(perm) WHERE p.perm LIKE 'workforce.%' ORDER BY r.role, p.perm; -> exactly 19 rows: five roles with three (view, manage, publish), three roles with one (finance, finance_manager, viewer), department_manager with two (publish, view), and three roles with none. **If department_manager appears with workforce.manage, stop.**
what_a_correct_result_looks_like.the_session_probe: SELECT count(*) FROM public.admin_acting_context_sessions WHERE revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now(); -> every one of these sessions is now INVALID. Each affected user must re-activate their acting context. Put this number in the release ticket so support knows the size of the re-login wave before users report it.
what_a_correct_result_looks_like.already_correct_is_correct: If a role's perms after the apply differ from the table above only in ARRAY ORDER, that is correct: the file writes a sorted union. Compare sets, not strings. If a role you expected to be created has no row, that is a FAILED apply — the post-condition would have raised.

The eight postflight probe results, each labelled with WHICH identity ran it. A probe run as the wrong identity is not evidence — in particular the department_manager probe must be run AS a department_manager, or as the superuser, and saying which.

SECURITY/ADMIN — this migration widens workforce.manage, and therefore staff_members INSERT and UPDATE, to five roles inside the organization: owner, admin, tour_manager, production, production_manager. That is CP-094's own sentence applied to the latter three by WFC-003's rule and it is the reason the apply is reviewed rather than accepted on the harness alone. The cross-tenant probes are the ones that matter and the harness cannot substitute for them on a real target.

WFC-003 / ORCHESTRATOR — the 206-pair residual OUTSIDE the workforce family is now a number, not a sentence: owner=37 admin=35 tour_manager=26 production=24 production_manager=24 department_manager=11 finance=13 finance_manager=14 ticketing=7 ticketing_manager=7 viewer=9 worker=0 (role, capability) pairs that the application gate grants and the matrix does not. Closing it means seeding the full catalog projection, which is a NEW CP authored by WFC-003 (HF-WFC-004 residual gap #1). This lane measured it and did not absorb it.

ORCHESTRATOR / RELEASE — WIRE THE TWO INSTRUMENTS. `npx vitest run __tests__/admin/db016-capability-matrix-agreement.test.ts` (7 tests, no database needed) and `bash supabase/tests/db016_workforce_role_seed.harness.sh` (64 checks, needs a local PostgreSQL 16) exist and are proven but run on nobody's behalf. Wiring them into package.json and the CI workflow is outside this lane's grant, and scripts/ci/ is DB-015's while it runs. This is the standing rule CP-110 asks for - a new capability is not shipped until the matrix grants it, and the two layers are compared in CI rather than reconciled by hand - and it is currently only a sentence.

DB-015 / ORCHESTRATOR — the residual 206 is exactly the failure class the new CP-110 detector should report on every migration that touches a capability catalog or a role matrix. This lane deliberately put the check in __tests__/ rather than in scripts/ci/ because that directory was owned by a concurrent lane; moving or re-implementing it is a one-file job once the ownership clears.

WFC-005 / WFC-006 — two residuals this migration deliberately did NOT solve and that the manifest now names: workforce.view is organization-wide at the RLS layer for department_manager (ADMIN-012's explicit decision), and workforce.publish is seeded for eight roles but read by NO RLS policy anywhere in the chain, so it currently changes no row-level access.
blockers: No hosted apply, no hosted postflight, no hosted probe and no hosted evidence exists, and the authoring lane could not produce any. Everything in this handoff is either static review of the active chain or a local emulation on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster: not Supabase, not a hosted project, not a chain replay, no `supabase db reset`, no `db push --include-all` (CP-051).

Whether the target's matrix already carries a workforce.* permission on some role cannot be answered from the chain, because DB-002 found out-of-band Management API application. Only the preflight can answer it, and the migration's exact-membership assertion will ABORT the apply if the answer is bad. That is the intended behaviour and it is a stop condition, not a failure to work around.

How many acting-context sessions a given target holds live, and whether the re-activation path works on it, are both unknown here. That is the single largest cost of this apply and it is why the re-activation walkthrough is a PREFLIGHT step.

Whether `authenticated` actually holds EXECUTE on public.has_perm on the hosted project is NOT verified. The chain grants it at 20260711153040:36 and the function is SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path, so the failure direction is an ERROR rather than a denial - loud, not silent, but still a stop condition.
